lines.japanese: 『レポート提出完了』
lines.english: “Paper submitted.”

lines.japanese:
『今日はこのままゼミの打ち上げ。
とは言っても四年やＭ２の先輩たちには、
クリスマスも正月もないんだろうけど』
lines.english: “We’re heading straight to the seminar party now. Though I doubt the fourth-years and second-year master’s students get either Christmas or New Year’s off.”

lines.japanese:
『それでも、こっちは晴れて冬休み入り。
年末年始は、今やってる二つのバイトに加えて、
短期のバイトも入れるか検討中』
lines.english: “The rest of us are officially on winter break. Along with my two current jobs, I’m considering taking another short-term one over the holidays.”

lines.japanese: 『...これじゃ俺も、クリスマスも正月もないな』
lines.english: “…Which means I won’t have Christmas or New Year’s either.”

lines.japanese:
『けど、今のうちに貯金しておかないと。
来年は就職活動でバイトもままならないし』
lines.english: “Still, I need to save while I can. Once job hunting starts next year, I won’t have much time to work.”

lines.japanese:
『雪菜は冬休み、どこか行く？
北海道でスキーとか、逆に沖縄とか。
それとも思い切って海外？』
lines.english: “Are you going anywhere over winter break? Skiing in Hokkaido, maybe, or somewhere warm like Okinawa? You could even go abroad.”

lines.japanese:
『...どうかな？　そういうのあまり想像できないな。
雪菜って見かけによらず出不精だもんな』
lines.english: “…I can’t really picture any of those. You don’t look it, but you’re quite the homebody.”

lines.japanese:
「クリスマスも正月もない、か。
...そんな完璧にガードしなくてもなぁ」
lines.english: “No break for Christmas or New Year’s… He really didn’t have to close off every possible opening.”

lines.japanese: 「せっかくの冬休みなのになぁ」
lines.english: “And after I finally got a winter break…”

lines.japanese: 「はぁぁぁぁ～」
lines.english: “Haaaaah…”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese:
「４時３５分...
まさかの５分遅刻...」
lines.english: “Four thirty-five. Five minutes late. Who could have imagined?”

lines.japanese:
「このあたしを待たせるとは、
い～い身分になったものよねぇ」
lines.english: “Making me wait—someone’s certainly gotten important.”

lines.japanese: 「晶子さん？」
lines.english: “Shouko?”

lines.japanese:
「...って、あたしが時間通りに来てるのがおかしいのか。
慣れないことするもんじゃないよねぇ」
lines.english: “No, wait. The truly strange thing is that I arrived on time. I should never do anything so out of character.”

lines.japanese: 「晶子さん...？」
lines.english: “Shouko…?”

lines.japanese:
「あ～、お腹空いた。
ちっくしょ～、打ち上げでは食べてやる。
あいつのおごりで食べまくってやる～」
lines.english: “God, I’m starving. Damn it, I’m eating everything at that party. I’ll gorge myself on his tab.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの～」
lines.english: “Um, excuse me…”
“Huh? Oh!”

lines.japanese:
「晶子さん...ですよね？
長瀬晶子さん」
lines.english: “You are Shouko Nagase, aren’t you?”

lines.japanese: 「しょうこ...？」
lines.english: “Shouko…?”

lines.japanese:
「わたしです、ほら、小木曽雪菜。
覚えてませんか？　この前のパーティで」
lines.english: “It’s me—Setsuna Ogiso. Don’t you remember? We met at that party.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、もしかして人違い...？」
lines.english: “Oh… Have I mistaken you for someone else?”

lines.japanese:
「っ！
あ、あ～！　そうそう晶子！
あたしってばそんな名前だったわ～！」
lines.english: “Oh! Right, of course—Shouko! That’s right—that was my name!”

lines.japanese:
「よ、よかったぁ...
恥ずかしい勘違いしたかと思っちゃった」
lines.english: “Thank goodness. I thought I’d made an incredibly embarrassing mistake.”

lines.japanese:
「ど、ど、どしたの？
今日はもう終わり？
それじゃお疲れ...」
lines.english: “S-so, what brings you here? Finished for the day? Well then, take care…”

lines.japanese:
「うん、これで今年の講義は全部終わり。
めでたくもあり、めでたくもない冬休みの始まり」
lines.english: “Yes, that was my last class of the year. Now begins my winter break, for better or worse.”

lines.japanese:
「そ、そう...それわよかった...
えっと、その...」
lines.english: “R-right. That’s… good. Um…”

lines.japanese:
「どうしたの？
この寒いのに、すごい汗」
lines.english: “Are you all right? You’re sweating terribly, and it’s freezing out here.”

lines.japanese: 「よくぞ遅刻してくれた春希...」
lines.english: “Thank God you’re late, Haruki…”

lines.japanese:
「ほら、ハンカチどうぞ。
もしかして体調でも悪い？
医務室まで付き添おうか？」
lines.english: “Here, use my handkerchief. Are you feeling ill? I could walk you to the clinic.”

lines.japanese:
「さすがのあたしにだって、
ごまかしきれる状況と、
そうでない状況があるのよねぇ...」
lines.english: “Even I have my limits. There are situations I can bluff my way through, and situations I simply can’t…”

lines.japanese: 「え？　なに？」
lines.english: “What was that?”

lines.japanese:
「ちょっと疲れたから一刻も早くここから離れない！？
...じゃなくて、再会を祝してお茶でも飲みに行かない？」
lines.english: “I’m exhausted, so can we get away from here immediately?! I mean—why don’t we celebrate meeting again by getting some tea?”

lines.japanese:
「はぁ、はぁ、はぁ...っ、
やべ、１０分遅刻」
lines.english: “Hah… hah… Damn, ten minutes late.”

lines.japanese: 「って、あれ？」
lines.english: “Wait. Where is she?”

lines.japanese: 「...やっぱり時間通りに来やがらねぇ」
lines.english: “…Of course she couldn’t arrive on time.”

lines.japanese:
「お待たせしました。
ストロベリーパフェとマンゴーパフェです。
...ごゆっくりどうぞ」
lines.english: “Thank you for waiting. One strawberry parfait and one mango parfait. Please enjoy.”

lines.japanese: 「わ～い、来た来た」
lines.english: “Yay, here they are!”

lines.japanese:
「勢いで頼んじゃったけど、
夕飯前にパフェなんていいのかなぁ」
lines.english: “I ordered on impulse, but should I really be eating a parfait right before dinner?”

lines.japanese:
「い～のい～の。
年に一度の忘年会なんだから」
lines.english: “Of course. It’s our one and only year-end party.”

lines.japanese:
「勢いで頼んじゃったけど、
忘年会にパフェってのも...ま、いいかぁ」
lines.english: “Still, parfaits for a year-end party are a little… Oh, who cares.”

lines.japanese:
「それじゃ、今年もお疲れさまでした。
かんぱ～い」
lines.english: “Here’s to all our hard work this year. Cheers!”

lines.japanese: 「わ、こぼれるこぼれる！」
lines.english: “Careful, you’re spilling it!”

lines.japanese: 「わ、おいし」
lines.english: “Oh, that’s delicious.”

lines.japanese:
「やっぱり寒い冬は
あったかいお店の中でパフェだよね～」
lines.english: “Nothing beats eating a parfait in a warm café on a cold winter day.”

lines.japanese: 「コタツに入ってバニラアイスに通じるものがあるよね」
lines.english: “It’s like eating vanilla ice cream curled up at a heated table.”

lines.japanese: 「あたしあれ大好き。雪菜は？」
lines.english: “I love doing that. Don’t you?”

lines.japanese:
「お徳用パックはいつも常備してるよ。
たまに弟が全部食べちゃって喧嘩になるけどね」
lines.english: “We always keep one of those big value tubs at home. Sometimes my brother eats the whole thing and we have a fight.”

lines.japanese: 「っ...なんて微笑ましい姉弟」
lines.english: “God, you two are adorable.”

lines.japanese:
「みんなそうやって笑うけどさぁ、
当事者たちにとっては死活問題なのよね。
『買って来ればいい』ってものじゃないし」
lines.english: “Everyone laughs, but it’s a matter of life and death when you’re involved. ‘Just buy another one’ entirely misses the point.”

lines.japanese:
「あ～、わかるわかる。
今、コタツの中でこそが食べたい瞬間で、
ちょっと経つとどうでもよくなっちゃうんだよね～」
lines.english: “Oh, I know exactly what you mean. You want it right then, while you’re all warm under the table. A little later, you don’t care anymore.”

lines.japanese:
「そうそう、寒い中コンビニに出かけてもさ、
結局買って帰るのは肉まんだったりして」
lines.english: “Exactly. If you go out to the convenience store in the cold, you end up coming home with a steamed pork bun instead.”

lines.japanese: 「当たり前じゃんねぇ。外寒いんだから」
lines.english: “Naturally. It’s freezing outside.”

lines.japanese:
「二つ買ってきてさ、
もちろん全部自分が食べるの。弟の前で」
lines.english: “So I buy two, and of course I eat both of them. Right in front of my brother.”

lines.japanese: 「...気持ちはわかるけど、根暗な復讐だ」
lines.english: “I understand the impulse, but that’s a very dark little revenge.”

lines.japanese:
「ん～、やっぱりおいし。
お店に入ってすぐに出てきても駄目なんだよね。
だいぶ体があったまった頃に出てきてもらわないと」
lines.english: “Mmm, this really is good. It wouldn’t be the same if they brought it as soon as you came in. You need to be thoroughly warm first.”

lines.japanese:
「？　どしたの？
わたしの顔、クリームでもついてる？」
lines.english: “What is it? Do I have cream on my face?”

lines.japanese:
「結構明るくなったかなって。
この前会った時と比べて」
lines.english: “You seem much brighter than the last time I saw you.”

lines.japanese:
「...そうかな？
別にそれほど変わらないと思うけどなぁ」
lines.english: “Do I? I don’t think I’ve changed much.”

lines.japanese: 「上手いこと行ってるんだ、彼と」
lines.english: “Things are going well with him, then.”

lines.japanese:
「変わってないって言ってるのに...
そもそもこの前から彼がいるなんて一言も...」
lines.english: “I just said I haven’t changed. Besides, I never told you I had a boyfriend…”

lines.japanese:
「あたしはさぁ、もう大変よぉ。
クリスマス合わせで新しい男見つけようって、
手当たり次第コナかけてるんだけどさぁ」
lines.english: “Me, I’m in crisis. I’ve been flirting with every man in sight, trying to find someone in time for Christmas.”

lines.japanese:
「勝手に納得して
次の話題に進まないで欲しいんだけどなぁ...」
lines.english: “Please don’t decide you’re right and move on before I can answer…”

lines.japanese:
「この電話は、現在電波の届かないところにあるか、
電源をお切りになっています」
lines.english: “The phone you are calling is either outside the service area or switched off.”

lines.japanese: 「何やってんだよあいつは...」
lines.english: “What the hell is she doing?”

lines.japanese: 現在、５時３０分。
lines.english: It was now five thirty.

lines.japanese:
打ち上げの場所がわからないって泣き言言うから、
４時半にキャンパスで待ち合わせたのに、
４５分過ぎても和泉は現れなかった。
lines.english: Izumi had complained that she couldn’t find the party venue, so we had arranged to meet on campus at four thirty. Forty-five minutes later, she still hadn’t appeared.

lines.japanese:
まぁ、『いつものこと』と言われれば、
そんなような気がしないでもないかもしれないけど、
それで連絡も取れないなんてのは、俺の常識にはない。
lines.english: Perhaps this was business as usual for her. I could almost accept that. But failing to show up and making herself unreachable as well lay outside any definition of normal I recognized.

lines.japanese: 「え～と、それじゃ飲み物行き渡りましたか～？」
lines.english: “All right, does everyone have a drink?”

lines.japanese:
今までゼミの行事を、課題提出含め全部スルーしてきた
和泉が、初めて打ち上げに参加してもいいってんで、
結構方々に調整で走り回ったんだけどなぁ。
lines.english: Izumi had ignored everything connected with the seminar so far, from submitting assignments to attending social events. When she finally said she might come to a party, I’d run all over the place making arrangements.

lines.japanese:
あの怠惰で気まぐれなじゃじゃ馬は、
やっぱり誰にも御しきれないんだろうか。
lines.english: Was that lazy, capricious wild mare simply beyond anyone’s power to tame?

lines.japanese:
...言い方は悪いけど、
俺にだけは懐いてくれてると思ったんだけどな。
lines.english: It sounds awful, but I’d thought I was the one person she’d grown attached to.

lines.japanese:
「はい、それじゃ乾杯の前に、
荻島先生から一言お願いします」
lines.english: “Before the toast, Professor Ogishima has a few words for us.”

lines.japanese:
「そいでさ、あたし言ってやったわけよ。
その『２３時からってのはなんなの？』って」
lines.english: “So I said to him, ‘What do you mean, eleven at night?’”

lines.japanese: 「お、遅いね」
lines.english: “Th-that is late.”

lines.japanese:
「さっきまで『新入社員だから時間作れる』って
言ってたその口が何を言うかって」
lines.english: “This from the same mouth that had just told me, ‘I’m a new hire, so I can always make time.’”

lines.japanese: 「そ、その日だけ忙しかったんじゃない？」
lines.english: “Maybe he was only busy that one day?”

lines.japanese:
「『その日』がクリスマスイブじゃなかったら、
こっちも納得しないでもなかったんだけどねぇ...」
lines.english: “I might have bought that if ‘that one day’ hadn’t been Christmas Eve.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あはは...」
lines.english: “Ahaha…”

lines.japanese:
「結局コイツも掛け持ちかよって、
また一瞬で醒めちゃって。
あたしの方から捨ててやったわよ、あんな男」
lines.english: “The instant I realized he was double-booking women, all my interest vanished. I dumped him on the spot.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええと...強い、のかな？」
lines.english: “Um… good for you?”

lines.japanese:
「結局、今年のクリスマスもシングル確定～。
あ～あ、もう、やんなっちゃうなぁ」
lines.english: “So I’m officially single for Christmas again. Oh, God, I’m so sick of this.”

lines.japanese:
「...そんなに落ち込まないでよ。
今日で今年の嫌なこと、全部忘れるんでしょ？」
lines.english: “Don’t be too depressed. We’re forgetting everything bad that happened this year today, remember?”

lines.japanese:
「そっか、忘年会だったね。
ま、こうして人に聞いてもらって
ウサを晴らすってのもアリか」
lines.english: “Right, this is our year-end party. Complaining until I feel better certainly counts.”

lines.japanese:
「うん、わたしならいつでも相手になるよ。
話聞くだけしかできないけど」
lines.english: “You can always complain to me. Listening is about all I can do, though.”

lines.japanese:
「うん、サンキュ。
でも、雪菜はいいよね～」
lines.english: “Thanks. Still, you have it good, Setsuna.”

lines.japanese:
「え？　え？　わたし？
なんで？」
lines.english: “Me? Why?”

lines.japanese: 「だぁってぇ、彼と上手く行ってるみたいでさ～」
lines.english: “Because things seem to be going so well with your man.”

lines.japanese:
「う、上手くなんて行ってないよぉ！
...じゃなくて、彼がいるなんて言ってないよ...」
lines.english: “I-it isn’t going well! I mean, I never said I had a boyfriend…”

lines.japanese:
「ホント自分で気づいてないの？
この前と比べて断然明るいよ、今日？」
lines.english: “You honestly haven’t noticed? You’re worlds more cheerful than the last time I saw you.”

lines.japanese: 「...って、どれだけやさぐれてたのよ、この前のわたし」
lines.english: “Just how wretched did I seem when we last met?”

lines.japanese:
「話してみ話してみ。
あたしは人の幸福話聞いても落ち込まないからさぁ。
...すでにどん底だからこれ以上落ちようがないし」
lines.english: “Tell me all about it. Other people’s happiness can’t drag me down. I’m already at rock bottom.”

lines.japanese:
「だからぁ、わたしはぁ...
この前のことだって、たとえ話だって何度も」
lines.english: “I told you—I told you over and over that everything I said last time was hypothetical.”

lines.japanese: 「あ～たとえ話でいいから、何でもいいから」
lines.english: “Then give me the hypothetical version. Anything will do.”

lines.japanese:
「人の言うこと頭から信じてないんだもんなぁ。
.........別に、一進一退だよ」
lines.english: “You refuse to believe a word I say. Fine… We take one step forward and one step back.”

lines.japanese: 「一進一退？」
lines.english: “One forward and one back?”

lines.japanese:
「...一度大喧嘩して、
その後メールで仲直りした」
lines.english: “We had a terrible fight, then made up by email.”

lines.japanese: 「なにそれ？　一進一退じゃん」
lines.english: “What do you know? One step forward and one step back.”

lines.japanese: 「だからそう言ってるのに...」
lines.english: “That’s what I just said…”

lines.japanese: 「ん～...なんだかなぁ」
lines.english: “Hmm… I don’t know.”

lines.japanese:
「ご期待に添えなくて悪うございました。
...勝手に期待して勝手にがっかりされても困るよ」
lines.english: “I deeply apologize for failing to entertain you. Though I can’t help it if you invent expectations and disappoint yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「ん～、んぅぅぅ～」
lines.english: “Mmm… hmmmm…”

lines.japanese:
「でも、今は一進一退だけど...
もしかしたら、今度こそは前に進めるかも」
lines.english: “Still, even if we’re going back and forth now… perhaps this time we really can move forward.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese:
「...なんてね。
勝手に期待して、勝手にがっかりしても悲しいし、
そういうこと、あまり想像しないようにしてるけど」
lines.english: “…Or maybe that’s just wishful thinking. It only hurts when I get my hopes up and let myself down, so I try not to imagine things like that.”
“Mmmmm…”

lines.japanese: 「晶子さん？」
lines.english: “Shouko?”

lines.japanese:
「っ！　できた～！
ほらほら見て見て！
サクランボの茎、口の中で結べたよ？」
lines.english: “I did it! Look, look! I tied the cherry stem in a knot with my tongue!”
“…Good for you.”

lines.japanese: 「北原ぁ、和泉さんいつになったら来るんだよ～？」
lines.english: “Kitahara, when is Izumi getting here?”

lines.japanese: 「すいません...連絡つかなくて」
lines.english: “Sorry. I can’t reach her.”

lines.japanese:
「彼女が来るってお前が言ったから、
今日帰省する予定をキャンセルして来たんだぞ～？」
lines.english: “I canceled my trip home today because you said she was coming.”

lines.japanese:
「...とっとと帰省すりゃ良かったじゃないですか。
別にそんなもん、飲み会に来る理由にならないでしょ」
lines.english: “Then you should have gone home. Wanting to see her is hardly a reason to come to a seminar party.”

lines.japanese:
和泉の打ち上げ出席宣言と結局のすっぽかしは、
男子ゼミ生の間に、結構な波紋を呼んでいたらしい。
lines.english: Izumi’s announcement that she would attend—and her ultimate failure to appear—had apparently caused quite a stir among the men in the seminar.

lines.japanese:
「なに？　やっぱお前ら付き合ってんだ？
彼女目当ての俺らウザい？」
lines.english: “What, are you two dating after all? Does it annoy you that we came for her?”

lines.japanese:
「.........俺とは関係なしに、
先輩たち、本当にあんなんがいいんですか？」
lines.english: “…Leaving me out of it, do you guys honestly like someone like her?”

lines.japanese: 「だってさぁ...ウチのゼミの中じゃダントツじゃん？」
lines.english: “Come on. She’s in a league of her own among the women in our seminar.”

lines.japanese:
今の台詞は声を潜めて欲しかった。
...正面に女性軍がいるってのに。
lines.english: I wished he had lowered his voice for that. The women were sitting directly across from us.

lines.japanese:
「可愛いと綺麗の中間くらいでさ、
あと、なんか雰囲気あるんだよな」
lines.english: “She’s somewhere between pretty and beautiful, and there’s just something about her.”

lines.japanese: ありますね...怠惰な雰囲気が。
lines.english: There was indeed something about her. An air of indolence.

lines.japanese: 前半に関してはコメントしないけど。
lines.english: I would offer no comment on the first half.

lines.japanese:
「結構フランクだし、話しやすいし。
一緒にいると楽しそうだって言うか」
lines.english: “She’s relaxed, easy to talk to. You get the feeling she’d be fun to have around.”

lines.japanese:
「...まぁ、ずっと一緒にいる奴に言っても
しょうがないけど」
lines.english: “Though there’s no point telling the man who spends all his time with her.”

lines.japanese:
「なら、先輩たちがあいつのレポート
手伝ってやれば良かったんじゃないですか」
lines.english: “Then one of you should have helped her write her paper.”

lines.japanese: 好きで一緒にいた訳じゃないのに...
lines.english: It wasn’t as if I’d spent that time with her because I wanted to.

lines.japanese: 「いや、それはない。俺の卒業がない」
lines.english: “Absolutely not. Then I’d never graduate.”

lines.japanese: 「...ごもっとも」
lines.english: “A fair point.”

lines.japanese:
まぁ、嫌なら一緒にいない選択肢も、
ないわけじゃなかったんだけどな。
lines.english: Though if I had truly hated it, choosing not to be with her had always been an option.

lines.japanese:
「それになぁ...
もう完全に、北原と和泉は付き合ってるって、
ゼミの中じゃ共通認識になってたし」
lines.english: “Besides, everyone in the seminar already assumed you and Izumi were dating.”

lines.japanese:
「ウチらの代の女たちが聞いてみたら、
本人、ゲラゲラ笑って否定しなかったって」
lines.english: “Some women in our year asked her. Apparently she just laughed her head off and never denied it.”

lines.japanese: 「それ、全然答えになってないじゃないですか」
lines.english: “That isn’t an answer at all.”

lines.japanese: いや...
lines.english: Or was it?

lines.japanese:
『心当たりないですか？
大学とか、別のバイト先とかでも、
いつの間にか公認扱いされてたりとか』
lines.english: “Can you honestly think of no other examples? At the university, perhaps, or your other job—people deciding you and some woman are a couple without either of you realizing?”

lines.japanese: こういうのも、俺のせいなんだろうか。
lines.english: Was this my fault too?

lines.japanese:
和泉が俺との関係を否定しないのも、
俺が和泉に曖昧な態度を示してしまうから...
lines.english: Was Izumi refusing to deny our supposed relationship because I had been ambiguous with her?

lines.japanese:
あいつとなら、そういう感覚を、
『お互い』抱かないだろうって信じてたけど。
lines.english: I had trusted that neither of us would ever look at the other that way.

lines.japanese:
そんな信頼、
本当に信頼と呼べる代物なんだろうか...？
lines.english: But could a belief like that really be called trust?

lines.japanese:
「くっそ～、つまらん。
ほら、もっと飲め北原」
lines.english: “Damn, this is no fun. Here, drink up, Kitahara.”

lines.japanese:
「次は俺の番な。
彼女が来ない分、お前が責任取るんだぞ？」
lines.english: “I’m next. Since she didn’t show, you have to make up for her.”

lines.japanese:
「...俺が救急車で運ばれたら、
先輩たちの就職に良くない影響が出ると思いますけど？」
lines.english: “If I leave here in an ambulance, it may reflect poorly on your job prospects.”

lines.japanese: 「...お前、前から思ってたけどヤな奴だな」
lines.english: “You know, I’ve thought this for a while: you’re a nasty piece of work.”

lines.japanese:
「ええ。
女なんか寄ってくる訳ないですよ...」
lines.english: “Exactly. No wonder women don’t come near me…”
“Nn…”
“Llr… mm… mmm…”

lines.japanese: 「ん、あ、あ...はんっ」
lines.english: “Mm… ah… ahh…”

lines.japanese:
「ぷぁぁっ...駄目だぁ。
やっぱり晶子さんみたいにはいかないよ」
lines.english: “Pwah… I can’t do it. I can’t do it the way you can.”

lines.japanese: 「...ごちそうさま」
lines.english: “…That was quite a treat.”

lines.japanese:
「どうしたらこんなの口の中で結べるようになるの？
いっつも練習してたりする？」
lines.english: “How do you tie one of these inside your mouth? Do you practice all the time?”

lines.japanese:
「これって、
キスの上手さに通じるものがあるって言うけどね」
lines.english: “They say it means you’re a good kisser.”
“K-kissing…?!”

lines.japanese:
「...なんてね。
口の中を自由に動かせればこんなの誰だってできるよ」
lines.english: “I’m teasing. Anyone can do it if they can move their tongue freely enough.”

lines.japanese: 「普通の人はそれができないんだけど...」
lines.english: “Most people can’t—that’s the entire problem.”

lines.japanese: 「にしても、堪能させていただきました」
lines.english: “In any case, I thoroughly enjoyed myself.”

lines.japanese: 「？　できなかったのに？」
lines.english: “Why? I failed.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、雪菜の色っぽい声と仕草をね」
lines.english: “I meant your sultry voice and all those little gestures.”
“…What?”

lines.japanese:
「あんなの目の前でやられたら、
男はたまったもんじゃないだろうねぇ」
lines.english: “Do that in front of a man and the poor creature wouldn’t stand a chance.”

lines.japanese: 「な、な、なんのこと...？」
lines.english: “Wh-what do you mean?”

lines.japanese:
「小さくすぼめた唇からちろっと顔を出すピンクの舌とか、
少しだけ苦しそうで少しだけ恍惚とした吐息とか」
lines.english: “That flash of pink tongue slipping between your pursed lips. Those little breaths, half strained and half ecstatic…”

lines.japanese: 「っ...い、いやらしいよ言い方が」
lines.english: “D-don’t describe it so obscenely!”

lines.japanese:
「雪菜の仕草の方がよっぽどいやらしいってば。
もう男を誘う要素満載。あたしと色気が違うよ色気が」
lines.english: “What you were doing was much filthier. Everything about it was an invitation. You’ve got a whole different kind of sex appeal than I do.”

lines.japanese:
「ちょ、ちょっとぉ、やめてよ。
そんなの意識してないってば！」
lines.english: “Stop it! I wasn’t trying to do anything like that!”

lines.japanese:
「ホント、すっごい勉強になる。
最高だよお師匠様」
lines.english: “Honestly, I’m learning so much from you. You’re one hell of a teacher.”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
「雪菜ってさ、会うたびに新発見があるんだよね。
ほんと、見てて面白い」
lines.english: “I discover something new every time I see you. You’re fascinating to watch.”

lines.japanese:
「わたしには、晶子さんの方が面白いけどなぁ。
話をしてても、全然先が読めないし」
lines.english: “I find you more fascinating. Whenever we talk, I can never predict what you’ll say next.”

lines.japanese:
「普通の男ならコロっといくに決まってるのにね。
...雪菜の彼って不感症なんじゃないの？」
lines.english: “Any normal man would fall for you instantly. Is your boyfriend completely numb?”

lines.japanese: 「...またその話？」
lines.english: “Are we back to that again?”

lines.japanese:
「何度も言うけどさぁ、あたしが男だったら、
絶対に放っとかないってこんな理想のコ。
...ううん、雪菜となら女同士でも」
lines.english: “I’ve said it before: if I were a man, I’d never let a perfect girl like you get away. No—with you, I might not even let being a woman stop me.”

lines.japanese: 「もう、晶子さんってばぁ」
lines.english: “Oh, Shouko…”

lines.japanese:
「なぁ、今度のクリスマス、一緒に過ごさないか？
三つ星レストランでフレンチを堪能して、
レインボーブリッジで夜景を眺めて...それからっ」
lines.english: “Setsuna, will you spend Christmas with me? We’ll dine at a three-star French restaurant, gaze at the lights from Rainbow Bridge, and then…”

lines.japanese: 「逆だよ...感受性が豊かだったんだ」
lines.english: “It was the opposite. He felt too much.”

lines.japanese: 「人のボケに付き合ってくれないし」
lines.english: “You aren’t even going to play along with the joke?”

lines.japanese:
「だから、いつまでも傷が癒えないんだ。
...わたしも自分も、許してくれないんだよ」
lines.english: “That’s why the wound never heals. He can’t forgive me—or himself.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
「...あ、いけない。
また変なこと喋っちゃった。
彼なんて、いないはずなのにね」
lines.english: “Oh, I shouldn’t have said that. There I go saying strange things again, when this ‘he’ isn’t even supposed to exist.”

lines.japanese:
「そろそろ帰らないと。
今日はありがとね、晶子さん」
lines.english: “I should be going. Thank you for today, Shouko.”

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、雪菜」
lines.english: “Hey, Setsuna.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「何年も一人の男を想い続けるって、どういう感じ？」
lines.english: “What does it feel like to love the same man for years?”
“…What are you talking about?”

lines.japanese:
「心当たりがなければ、別にいいんだけどね。
ただ参考までに聞いてみただけだし」
lines.english: “If nothing comes to mind, forget it. I was only taking notes.”

lines.japanese:
「...行こうか。
あたしおごるよ。二人の再会を祝して」
lines.english: “Let’s go. My treat, to celebrate our reunion.”

lines.japanese: 「わたしも祝いたいから、ワリカンでどう？」
lines.english: “I want to celebrate too. Why don’t we split it?”
“All right.”

lines.japanese: 「行こうか」
lines.english: “Shall we?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese:
「どういう感じかと聞かれても、
そんなのわかんないよ」
lines.english: “I don’t know what it feels like.”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
「だって、その意味を考えたこともないし、
ずっと想い続けようって、努力したこともないんだから。
...ただの結果論だよ」
lines.english: “I’ve never stopped to think about what it means, and I’ve never had to work at loving him all these years. It’s just how things turned out.”
“Setsuna…”

lines.japanese:
「あ、でもさ、逆の努力は何度でもしたかな。
...忘れるための、ね」
lines.english: “Oh, but I did try the opposite plenty of times. I tried to forget him.”

lines.japanese: 「...やっぱあんた、男にとって毒だよ」
lines.english: “You really are poison to men.”

lines.japanese:
「和泉！
お前、今まで携帯も切って何やってたんだよ！」
lines.english: “Izumi! Where have you been, and why was your phone off?”

lines.japanese:
「...ごめん。
ちょっと中てられてた、というか、
ものすごく濃い特訓してた」
lines.english: “Sorry. I got a little overwhelmed, I guess. Or maybe I was getting one hell of an intensive lesson.”

lines.japanese: 「.........言ってる意味がわからないんだが？」
lines.english: “…I have no idea what that means.”

lines.japanese: 「...わかんないだろうねぇ」
lines.english: “No. I don’t suppose you would.”

lines.japanese: 約束の待ち合わせ時間から２時間後...
lines.english: Two hours after we were supposed to meet…

lines.japanese:
大遅刻の末にかかってきた携帯からは、
なんだか妙に堪能したというか、
そんな、ちょっとぼうっとした和泉の声が聞こえてきた。
lines.english: When Izumi finally called, two hours late, her voice sounded oddly sated—almost dazed.

lines.japanese:
「まぁいいや。場所わかるか？
なんなら迎えに行ってもいいけど」
lines.english: “Never mind. Do you know where the place is? I can come get you if you want.”

lines.japanese: 「まだやってんの？　打ち上げ」
lines.english: “Is the party still going?”

lines.japanese:
「店は９時までって話だから、まだ大丈夫だ。
それにどうせ二次会とかもあるんだろうし」
lines.english: “We have the restaurant until nine, so there’s plenty of time. There’ll probably be an after-party anyway.”
“I see…”

lines.japanese:
「どうした？
もしかして、来れなくなった？」
lines.english: “What’s wrong? Can’t you make it?”

lines.japanese:
「あ、ううん、
そういう訳じゃないんだけどさ...」
lines.english: “No, it isn’t that…”
“Izumi?”

lines.japanese: 「ん～...どしよっかなぁ」
lines.english: “Hmm… What should I do?”

lines.japanese: やっぱり今の和泉の態度はどこか変だ。
lines.english: There was definitely something strange about her.

lines.japanese:
倦怠感というか、恍惚感というか、
いつも以上にだらりとした言動が、
いつも以上に俺のテンポとずれる。
lines.english: She sounded more languid than usual, almost enraptured. Her words drifted even farther out of step with mine than usual.

lines.japanese:
「春希はさぁ、どうすんの？
一次会終わったら」
lines.english: “What are you doing when the party here ends, Haruki?”

lines.japanese: 「まぁ今日くらいは二次会付き合ってもいいけど」
lines.english: “I suppose I could join the after-party tonight, for once.”

lines.japanese: 「和泉？」
lines.english: “Izumi?”

lines.japanese: 「そっち、みんないるんだよねぇ？」
lines.english: “Everyone’s there with you, right?”

lines.japanese:
「打ち上げなんだから当たり前だろ。
いつも来ないのはお前くらいだ」
lines.english: “It’s a seminar party. Of course they are. You’re the only one who never shows up.”

lines.japanese: やっぱ変だ。
lines.english: Something was definitely wrong.

lines.japanese:
いつもはテンポはずれるんだけど、
会話の流れはきちんと掴んでて、
そこがまた心地良くさせてくれる奴なのに。
lines.english: Her timing was always eccentric, but she normally understood the current of a conversation perfectly. That was part of what made talking to her so easy.

lines.japanese:
今日は空気を読んでないというか、
俺を相手にしていないというか...
lines.english: Today it was as if she couldn’t read the room—or as if she weren’t really talking to me at all.

lines.japanese: 「春希さぁ」
lines.english: “Haruki…”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「抜けて来れない？」
lines.english: “Can’t you slip away?”

lines.japanese: 「意味がわからん」
lines.english: “I don’t understand.”

lines.japanese:
「二次会、二人きりでやんない？
...って意味なんだけど」
lines.english: “Why don’t we have our own after-party? Just the two of us.”

lines.japanese: 「...意味がわからん」
lines.english: “…I still don’t understand.”

lines.japanese:
「駄目かなぁ。
会いたいんだけどなぁ、今すぐ」
lines.english: “Is that a no? I want to see you. Right now.”

lines.japanese:
「っ...だったら今すぐこっちに来いよ。
みんな待ってるんだぞ？」
lines.english: “Then come here right now. Everyone is waiting for you.”

lines.japanese: 「春希、空気読めてない」
lines.english: “You’re the one who can’t take a hint, Haruki.”

lines.japanese: ほら、空気読めてない。
lines.english: There it was. She was the one who couldn’t take a hint.

lines.japanese:
「それはお前だ。
なに急に訳のわからんワガママ言ってやがる」
lines.english: “You’re the one who can’t. Why are you suddenly making these incomprehensible demands?”

lines.japanese:
でも、俺を相手にしていないって方の推測は、
これは大はずれ...なんだろうか？
lines.english: But perhaps I had been entirely wrong about her not really talking to me.

lines.japanese:
「どうしても駄目？
今でなくちゃいけないんだけど」
lines.english: “Do you absolutely have to say no? It has to be now.”

lines.japanese:
「何がだよ？
何言ってるんだ、お前？」
lines.english: “What does? What are you talking about?”

lines.japanese:
『二人きりになりたい』って...
別に、そんな言葉に動揺するような関係じゃない。
lines.english: “I want to be alone with you”… We didn’t have the kind of relationship where words like that should unsettle me.

lines.japanese: この一月、何度も部屋に上がり込んできた。
lines.english: She had invited herself into my apartment again and again over the past month.

lines.japanese:
付き合っていないくせに、
何時間も、何十時間も二人きりでいた。
lines.english: We weren’t dating, yet we had spent hours—dozens of hours—alone together.

lines.japanese: それなのに...
lines.english: And still…

lines.japanese:
「ね？　いいじゃん。
鉄は熱いうちに打てって言うじゃん...」
lines.english: “Please? Strike while the iron’s hot and all that…”

lines.japanese: 「だから、俺にわかるように説明しろ」
lines.english: “Then explain it in a way I can understand.”

lines.japanese:
なんで今日に限って、
和泉も、俺も、妙にこだわるんだろう。
lines.english: Why were both of us so strangely insistent tonight?

lines.japanese: １．やっぱりこっち来いよ
lines.english: 1. On second thought, come here.

lines.japanese: ２．今からそっち行くから
lines.english: 2. I’ll come to you now.

lines.japanese: 「先輩たち、和泉と飲みたがってるぞ」
lines.english: “The others want to drink with you too.”

lines.japanese:
和泉がこだわる理由は結局よくわからないけど、
俺が和泉の誘いを断る理由には、
なんとなく心当たりがあった。
lines.english: I still didn’t understand why Izumi was insisting, but I thought I understood why I was refusing.

lines.japanese:
「教授とだって、まともに話したことないだろ？
あと一年以上付き合うんだからさ、
そろそろ顔出しといた方がいいんじゃないか？」
lines.english: “You’ve never even had a proper conversation with the professor, have you? You’ll be in the seminar for more than another year. It’s about time you made an appearance.”

lines.japanese: 最近、和泉と上手に付き合えなくなりかけてる。
lines.english: Lately, I had been losing the knack of being around Izumi.

lines.japanese:
いや、関係的には今まで以上に良好なんだけど、
だからこそ、踏み外してしまいそうというか。
lines.english: No—our friendship was better than ever. That was precisely why I felt in danger of stepping over some line.

lines.japanese:
「俺と飲む機会なんて、
これからだっていくらでもあるし」
lines.english: “You’ll have plenty of other chances to drink with me.”

lines.japanese: 和泉が『女』になりかけてる。
lines.english: Izumi was becoming a woman in my eyes.

lines.japanese:
...いや、もしかしたらあっちは変わってないのに、
俺の方がそう感じるようになってしまってるのかも。
lines.english: Or perhaps she hadn’t changed at all. Perhaps I was the one who had begun to see her differently.

lines.japanese: 「ゲームオーバー、か」
lines.english: “Game over, then.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　何だって？」
lines.english: “What did you say?”

lines.japanese:
「いや、いいわ。
帰る」
lines.english: “Nothing. Forget it. I’m going home.”
“I see.”

lines.japanese:
そんな後ろめたい理由だからこそ、
和泉のその決断を、引き留めることなんかできない。
lines.english: Because my reasons filled me with guilt, I couldn’t ask her to change her mind.

lines.japanese:
そんな後ろめたい理由だからこそ、
正直に話してしまうこともできない。
lines.english: And because they filled me with guilt, I couldn’t tell her the truth.

lines.japanese:
「みんなに謝っといてね。
体調が悪くなっちゃったからとか適当な理由つけて」
lines.english: “Apologize to everyone for me. Tell them I felt sick or make up some other excuse.”

lines.japanese:
「任せとけ。
和泉が直接言うならともかく、
俺からの伝聞ならみんな信用する」
lines.english: “Leave it to me. If you told them yourself they’d never believe you, but they’ll trust it secondhand from me.”

lines.japanese: 和泉に指差して笑われるのが嫌だから。
lines.english: Because I didn’t want Izumi pointing at me and laughing.

lines.japanese:
「ひっど...
相変わらず春希は、女に冷たい男だね～」
lines.english: “Cruel. You’re as cold to women as ever.”
“Sorry.”

lines.japanese:
和泉が、くすっと笑いながら
受け入れてしまうのが怖いから。
lines.english: Because I was afraid she might accept the truth with a quiet little laugh.

lines.japanese:
「そんじゃね、おやすみ。
あまり飲み過ぎないようにね」
lines.english: “Good night, then. Don’t drink too much.”

lines.japanese:
「大丈夫だ。
俺、酒に関しては飲みたいだけ飲んでも、
絶対に自分で勝手にブレーキかけるから」
lines.english: “I’ll be fine. No matter how much I drink, something in me always applies the brakes on its own.”

lines.japanese: 「７０過ぎのおじいさんみたいだよそれ...」
lines.english: “You sound like a man in his seventies.”

lines.japanese: 「おやすみ」
lines.english: “Good night.”
“Mm.”

lines.japanese:
なんとなく湿っぽい雰囲気に後ろ髪を引かれつつ、
俺たちは、会話の終わった受話器を耳に当て続け...
lines.english: Reluctant to abandon the sudden melancholy between us, we both kept our silent phones pressed to our ears after the conversation had ended.

lines.japanese:
「ま、がんばりなよ。
結構めんどいコだよねぇ？　ご愁傷様」
lines.english: “Well, good luck. She sounds like quite a handful. My condolences.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 最後に、もう一つだけ訳のわからない謎を残した。
lines.english: And so she left me with one final, incomprehensible mystery.

lines.japanese:
『レポート提出お疲れさま。
今は打ち上げの真っ最中なのかな？
あまり飲み過ぎないようにね』
lines.english: “Congratulations on finishing your paper. Are you in the middle of the party now? Don’t drink too much.”

lines.japanese:
『かくいうわたしの方も、
さっきまで友達と打ち上げしてました』
lines.english: “As it happens, I was having a little year-end party of my own with a friend until just now.”

lines.japanese: 『...って言っても、喫茶店でパフェだけどね』
lines.english: “Though ours was only parfaits at a café.”

lines.japanese:
『相手は、先週知り合った長瀬さん。
相変わらず、美人なのに話すとすごく面白い人で、
二時間くらいお喋りであっという間に過ぎちゃった』
lines.english: “I went with Nagase, the woman I met last week. She’s still beautiful and incredibly funny once you talk to her. Two hours of chatting flew by.”

lines.japanese: 『さてと、春希くんお尋ねの冬休みの予定ですが...』
lines.english: “Now, to answer your question about my plans for winter break…”

lines.japanese:
『む～、出不精はひどいなぁ。
わたし、旅行は嫌いじゃないよ？
ただ、あまり忙しなく動くのが苦手なだけで』
lines.english: “Calling me a homebody is unfair. I don’t dislike traveling. I only dislike rushing frantically from place to place.”

lines.japanese:
『旅先で、ゆっくりお風呂に浸かって、
美味しいご飯食べて、楽しくお喋りできれば大満足』
lines.english: “Give me a long soak in a hot bath, a delicious meal, and someone I enjoy talking to, and I’ll be perfectly happy.”

lines.japanese:
『あと、移動に疲れないところがいいな。
車に乗っけてもらうとか、駅前すぐの旅館とか、
それに、荷物が重いのも嫌だから一泊くらいで』
lines.english: “Somewhere easy to reach would be nice. A place someone can drive me to, or an inn right outside the station. And I hate heavy luggage, so one night would be plenty.”

lines.japanese: 『あれ？　やっぱり出不精なのかなぁ、わたし』
lines.english: “Oh dear. Perhaps I am a homebody after all.”

lines.japanese:
『...そういえば昔、そんな旅、したよね？
楽しかったよね、すごく』
lines.english: “Come to think of it, we took a trip like that once, didn’t we? It was wonderful.”

lines.japanese: 『ね、春希くん』
lines.english: “Wasn’t it, Haruki?”

lines.japanese:
『春希くんに比べると、今のわたしは、
無精とか怠け者に見えるかもしれない。
でも、実は微妙に違うんだよ』
lines.english: “Compared with you, I might seem idle or lazy now. But the truth is slightly different.”

lines.japanese:
『ただ、もう頑張りたくないだけ。
楽に、なりたいだけなの』
lines.english: “I just don’t want to keep trying anymore. I only want some peace.”

lines.japanese: 楽に、なりたいだけ、か。
lines.english: She only wanted some peace.

lines.japanese:
誰なんだろうな。
今まで雪菜に楽をさせなかったのは。
lines.english: Who was it who had denied Setsuna even that?

lines.japanese: ずっと、苦しめ続けていた重罪人は。
lines.english: Who was the criminal who had made her suffer all these years?

lines.japanese:
「おい！　いつまでメール見てニヤニヤしてんだよ？
ちょっと見せてみろ」
lines.english: “Hey! How long are you going to sit there grinning at that email? Let me see.”

lines.japanese:
「あ...っ！？
や、やめろ！
...じゃなくてやめてくださいっ！」
lines.english: “Ah—! Stop it! I mean, please stop!”

lines.japanese:
「なんだ～？　もしかして和泉からか？
打ち上げ抜け出して、二人きりで会おうとか
密約してんじゃないだろうな？」
lines.english: “What is it—from Izumi? Are you secretly arranging to sneak out and meet her alone?”

lines.japanese:
「ちっ...！
違いますってば！
そっちはさっきちゃんと断って...」
lines.english: “No! I already turned her down when she asked me earlier…”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 俺の体は、途中から必死でブレーキをかけていた。
lines.english: At some point, my body began frantically applying the brakes.

lines.japanese:
なのに喉を通る酒はとどまるところを知らず、
救急車とはいかないまでも、
トイレの住人にはなってしまった。
lines.english: The liquor kept pouring down my throat regardless. I didn’t quite end up in an ambulance, but I did become a permanent resident of the bathroom.

lines.japanese:
「じゃあ、今から３０分後。
御宿の東口改札で」
lines.english: “Thirty minutes from now. The east ticket gate at Onjuku Station.”

lines.japanese: 「...いんだね？」
lines.english: “You’re… sure?”

lines.japanese: 「この前、おごるって約束したからな」
lines.english: “I promised to treat you, remember?”
“Haruki…”

lines.japanese: 多分、二人とも気づいてる。
lines.english: We probably both knew.

lines.japanese:
あの時の約束は、和泉が結局泊まってったことで、
とっくに意味のないものになっているって。
lines.english: That promise had lost any meaning the moment Izumi ended up staying the night.

lines.japanese:
「今度はすっぽかすなよ。
俺、さっき１時間近く待ったんだからな」
lines.english: “Don’t stand me up this time. I waited almost an hour for you earlier.”

lines.japanese:
「さっきのは.........わかった。
絶対に行くよ」
lines.english: “About that… All right. I promise I’ll come.”

lines.japanese:
だけど、二人とも蒸し返さないのは、
そんなことをして幸せになる人間が、
誰もいないから。
lines.english: But neither of us brought up what had happened, because doing so would make no one happy.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ、後で」
lines.english: “See you soon.”
“Mm.”

lines.japanese: 俺たち二人の間には。
lines.english: Not between the two of us.
“Now, then…”

lines.japanese: 「あたしは、誰？」
lines.english: “Who am I?”

lines.japanese:
「わたしです、ほら、小木曽雪菜。
覚えてませんか？　この前のパーティで」
lines.english: “It’s me—Setsuna Ogiso. Don’t you remember? We met at that party.”

lines.japanese:
「あれと同等以上の女を演じなきゃならないなんて、
なんてハードルの高い男だろうねぇ、春希くん」
lines.english: “So I have to play a woman who can match her—or top her? You set one hell of a high bar, Haruki.”

lines.japanese: 「...やりがいあるよね」
lines.english: “Now this is a challenge.”

lines.japanese:
「よしっ！
気合入れて行こう」
lines.english: “All right! Time to give it everything.”

lines.japanese:
「お疲れさまでした～！
ほ～ら、ぐっといって、ぐっと！」
lines.english: “Cheers to a job well done! Come on—drink up, drink up!”
“Uh… right.”

lines.japanese:
「んぐ、んぐ...
バーテンさん、マンハッタンおかわり～！」
lines.english: “Glug, glug… Bartender, another Manhattan!”

lines.japanese: 「いきなり店の雰囲気ぶち壊すな」
lines.english: “Don’t ruin the atmosphere the second we walk in.”

lines.japanese:
和泉と入ったのは、
今まで飲んでた居酒屋とは完全に趣を変えた、
雰囲気のよさそうなショットバー。
lines.english: Izumi and I had entered a stylish cocktail bar, a complete change from the noisy pub where I’d spent the evening.

lines.japanese:
...だったのに、肝心の和泉の方は、
居酒屋のテンションだった。
lines.english: Izumi herself, however, was still in rowdy-pub mode.

lines.japanese:
「春希もガンガンいきなよ。
どうせあんたのおごりなんだし～」
lines.english: “Drink up, Haruki. You’re paying for all of it anyway.”

lines.japanese:
「俺はさっきまでしこたま飲んできたんだよ。
...つか、本気で俺に全部おごらせる気か？」
lines.english: “I’ve already drunk a small ocean tonight. And are you seriously planning to make me pay for everything?”

lines.japanese:
あの時の約束はとっくに無効になってるって、
蒸し返そうかな...
lines.english: Maybe I should point out that our old promise had long since expired.

lines.japanese:
なんて半分頭を抱えつつ、
でも俺は、半分胸をなで下ろしていた。
lines.english: Half of me despaired at the thought. The other half was profoundly relieved.

lines.japanese:
「ほんとお疲れ。
あと、悪かったね無理に連れ出して」
lines.english: “Seriously, though—you’ve had a long day. And sorry I dragged you away like that.”

lines.japanese:
「あとで俺の言い訳を伝授しとくからな。
先輩たちに聞かれた時、ちゃんと口裏合わせろよ」
lines.english: “I’ll tell you later what excuse I gave them. If anyone asks, make sure our stories match.”

lines.japanese:
「大丈夫だって。
どうせこれで年明けまで大学行かないし～」
lines.english: “It’ll be fine. I’m not going back to campus until after New Year’s anyway.”

lines.japanese:
さっきの電話の和泉がそのまま来られたら、
自分がどう振舞えばいいのか決めかねていた。
lines.english: If Izumi had shown up sounding the way she did on the phone, I wouldn’t have known how to act.

lines.japanese: けどこれは、いつも通りのふざけた飲み会。
lines.english: But this was our usual ridiculous night of drinking.

lines.japanese:
俺がつまみを作り、酒を用意して、
和泉は飲んで騒ぐだけの、不公平な宴席。
lines.english: The same unfair feast where I made the food and poured the drinks while Izumi did nothing but drink and make noise.

lines.japanese:
だったら何も遠慮することはない。
散々たかられ、搾り取られた後に、
説教で少しだけ溜飲を下げれば万事解決。
lines.english: Then I had nothing to worry about. After she’d mooched off me and bled me dry, I could vent a little by lecturing her. Problem solved.

lines.japanese:
そうだよ...
だってそれが、俺たちの流儀なんだから。
lines.english: Yes. That was simply how the two of us worked.

lines.japanese: 「なぁ、和泉」
lines.english: “Hey, Izumi.”

lines.japanese: 目の前に、また新しいグラスが置かれる。
lines.english: Another fresh glass appeared in front of me.

lines.japanese:
俺がグラスを空けるたびに、
和泉が勝手に追加オーダーを飛ばしてしまうから。
lines.english: Every time I emptied one, Izumi ordered the next without asking.

lines.japanese:
...まだ自分の中のブレーキも作動しないのをいいことに、
それを次から次へと空ける俺にも
問題があるかもしれないけど。
lines.english: Though perhaps I was equally at fault. My brakes still hadn’t kicked in, and I kept knocking back every glass she sent my way.
“Mmm…?”

lines.japanese:
逆に、和泉の方が先に限界が近いのか、
さっきからカクテルに添えられたチェリーを
口に含むだけで、グラスが空かなくなった。
lines.english: Izumi seemed closer to her limit. For some time now, she had only been putting the cocktail cherries into her mouth; the drink itself remained untouched.

lines.japanese:
...とはいえ、こいつの重ねた杯数に追いつくには、
あと２杯飲む必要があるけど。
lines.english: Even so, I needed two more glasses to catch up with her total.

lines.japanese: ...ピッチ早。
lines.english: She drank fast.

lines.japanese:
「お前さぁ、
学園時代、どんな奴だったわけ？」
lines.english: “What were you like in high school?”

lines.japanese: 「...なんでそんなこと聞くの？　いきなり」
lines.english: “Why ask that out of nowhere?”

lines.japanese:
「別にいきなりじゃないだろ。
前から何度か聞いてたと思うけど？」
lines.english: “It isn’t out of nowhere. I’ve asked you before.”

lines.japanese: きっかけは、あの『昔のレポート』。
lines.english: The question had begun with that old paper of hers.

lines.japanese:
北陸地方の民話なんていう、
かなり資料を探すのも大変そうな、
しかも地味な研究をしていた学生時代。
lines.english: In high school, she had researched folk tales from the Hokuriku region—an obscure subject whose sources must have been painfully difficult to find.

lines.japanese:
今の、怠惰で要領良くて人間として軽い和泉は、
いつ形づくられたんだろうって、
失礼な疑問が頭に浮かぶのは当然だと思う。
lines.english: When had the Izumi I knew now—lazy, shrewd, and frivolous to her bones—taken shape? However rude it was, the question felt inevitable.

lines.japanese: いや、当然だと思うことが失礼に当たるんだろうか？
lines.english: Or was thinking I had every right to wonder the rudest part of all?

lines.japanese:
「確か都立だったよな。
どこだっけ？」
lines.english: “You went to a Tokyo public school, didn’t you? Which one?”
“Higashi-Arikawa?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、千葉に近い方？」
lines.english: “Oh, the one near Chiba?”

lines.japanese: にしても、なんで語尾を上げるんだろう。
lines.english: Why had she answered with a question?

lines.japanese:
「話してもいいけどさぁ、
別につまんないよ？」
lines.english: “I can tell you, but it won’t be very interesting.”

lines.japanese: 「お前と話してて、つまらないと思ったことないよ」
lines.english: “I’ve never been bored talking to you.”

lines.japanese: 「あ...ごめん」
lines.english: “Oh… sorry.”

lines.japanese: なんか和泉の肩がぴくんと震えたような気がした。
lines.english: I thought I saw Izumi’s shoulder twitch.

lines.japanese:
だから俺は、自分の吐いた台詞の意味もろくろく考えず、
ただ、その妙な反応に過剰反応を返した。
lines.english: Without stopping to consider the meaning of what I’d said, I overreacted to her strange reaction.

lines.japanese: 「ううん、けっこ嬉しいかも」
lines.english: “No. I think that made me happy.”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese: 「...謝ろっか？」
lines.english: “Would you like me to apologize?”

lines.japanese: 「...いや、別に」
lines.english: “No. It’s fine.”

lines.japanese:
和泉の右手が、カウンターの上に置かれた俺の左手に、
そっと重ねられる。
lines.english: Izumi gently laid her right hand over my left, where it rested on the counter.

lines.japanese: けどそれは、いつもの和泉の悪ふざけ。
lines.english: But this was only Izumi’s usual teasing.

lines.japanese:
軽くつねったり、爪で引っかいたり、
スキンシップだか悪戯だかわからない、
ほんのちょっとしたじゃれ合い。
lines.english: A pinch, a scrape of her nails—some tiny game halfway between affection and mischief.

lines.japanese:
だから俺は、過剰反応したりしない。
だって、男と女じゃなくて、友達同士の触れ合いだから。
lines.english: So I wasn’t going to overreact. This wasn’t a man and a woman touching. It was two friends.

lines.japanese:
『指相撲やろう？　１２３４５６７８９１０！』とか、
『指四の字～』とか『どっちの手が大きいかな？』とか、
そういったレベルの...
lines.english: “Let’s thumb-wrestle—one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!” Or, “Figure-four finger lock!” Or, “Let’s see whose hand is bigger.” That sort of thing.

lines.japanese: 「な、なぁ、和泉...」
lines.english: “H-hey, Izumi…”
“…Would you like me to apologize?”

lines.japanese:
「い、いや...
謝らなくてもいいけど、意図を説明して欲しいなと」
lines.english: “N-no… You don’t have to apologize. I’d just like to know what you meant by it.”

lines.japanese: 「なんとなく春希をいじってみたくなっただけ」
lines.english: “I simply felt like teasing you.”
“R-right…”

lines.japanese: そういったレベルの、はずなんだけど。
lines.english: It was supposed to be that sort of thing.

lines.japanese: なんか、違う...？
lines.english: But was it?

lines.japanese:
いつもの和泉と、手触りが違う。
...いや、正確に言えば、手触られ、だけど。
lines.english: Izumi felt different to the touch—or, strictly speaking, her touching me did.

lines.japanese: 「どこにでもいる、普通の女の子だったよ」
lines.english: “I was an ordinary girl. The kind you could find anywhere.”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
「都立の時代のあたし。
...なに春希？　自分で聞いたことすっかり忘れてる？」
lines.english: “Back when I went to a public high school. Did you completely forget the question you asked?”

lines.japanese: 「べ、別に」
lines.english: “Of course not.”

lines.japanese: いつもの和泉と、手の動きが違う。
lines.english: The movement of her hand was different too.

lines.japanese:
「学校の中じゃ目立たなくて。
だから、同じ学年のコにも覚えててもらえなかったり」
lines.english: “I never stood out. Sometimes people in my own year didn’t even remember me.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そう、か」
lines.english: “I-I see.”

lines.japanese:
つねったり、引っかいたり、
指相撲したり、指四の字したりせずに、
ただ、俺の手の甲に、自分の手のひらを重ねる。
lines.english: She didn’t pinch me or scratch me, didn’t start a thumb war or twist my fingers into a lock. She merely rested her palm on the back of my hand.

lines.japanese: その手触りも、繊細で、滑らかで、柔らかくて。
lines.english: Her touch was delicate, smooth, and soft.

lines.japanese:
いつもの力強さ...って言うか、
俺の照れと躊躇を誘発しないための気遣いがない。
lines.english: It lacked her usual forcefulness—or rather, the consideration behind it: never giving me a chance to feel shy or hesitate.

lines.japanese:
でもそれは、いつもより乱暴な訳じゃなく、
ただ、いつもより優しい、
けれどいつもより踏み込んだ触れ合い。
lines.english: This wasn’t rougher than usual. It was gentler, yet somehow far more intimate.

lines.japanese: だから、いつもみたいに邪魔そうに振り払えない。
lines.english: So I couldn’t shake her off with my usual show of annoyance.

lines.japanese:
困惑と羞恥と、そして少しの安心感とともに、
ただ、あるがままの状況を受け入れる。
lines.english: Confused, embarrassed, and a little reassured, I simply accepted things as they were.

lines.japanese:
「うん、そうだね。
部活はそれなりにやってたかな」
lines.english: “Let’s see… I was fairly serious about my club, I suppose.”
“Really…”

lines.japanese:
「結構なもんだったんだよ？
三年の時には、賞ももらったんだから」
lines.english: “I was quite good, actually. I even won an award in my final year.”

lines.japanese:
「そりゃ凄いな。
何部に入ってた？」
lines.english: “That is impressive. What club?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあね...当ててみて？」
lines.english: “Why don’t you guess?”

lines.japanese: 「っ...ヒントを」
lines.english: “Give me a hint.”

lines.japanese: 俺の杯数が、和泉に追いついた頃。
lines.english: By the time my drink count caught up with hers,

lines.japanese:
和泉の、ぽわっと赤らんだ瞳が、
俺を無遠慮に覗き込む。
lines.english: Izumi peered openly into my eyes, her own glazed and glowing with drink.

lines.japanese: 「ヒントねぇ...じゃ」
lines.english: “A hint? Well, then…”

lines.japanese:
和泉は、さっきまで舐めていたさくらんぼの実から、
茎だけ引き抜くと、指ごと口の中に押し込んだ。
lines.english: She plucked the stem from the cherry she had been sucking and pushed it into her mouth along with her fingers.

lines.japanese: 「...それに何の意味があるんだ？」
lines.english: “What is that supposed to mean?”

lines.japanese:
小さくすぼめた唇が自らの指を咥え込み、
軽い唾液の音を響かせる。
lines.english: Her pursed lips closed around her own fingers with a soft, wet sound.

lines.japanese: 「ん～、こんなでどう？」
lines.english: “Mmm. How’s this?”

lines.japanese: 「口の中で結ぼうってのか？」
lines.english: “You’re going to tie it in your mouth?”
“Mm.”

lines.japanese:
和泉は返事の代わりに、
こくんと頷きながら、
口の中をゆっくりと動かし始める。
lines.english: Izumi nodded and slowly began working the stem around in her mouth, answering me without words.

lines.japanese: じっと俺を見つめたままで。
lines.english: Her eyes never left mine.

lines.japanese: 「で、それが出来るとどうなんだ？」
lines.english: “And what does that have to do with the answer?”

lines.japanese:
「こういうのが役に立つ部だったんだよ。
ほら、よく見てみ？」
lines.english: “It was the kind of club where this skill came in handy. Here—watch closely.”

lines.japanese:
そう言うと和泉は、口を半開きにしたまま、
舌をもごもごと動かし、茎結びを始める。
lines.english: With her lips still parted, she moved her tongue slowly and began tying the stem.

lines.japanese: 「さて、答えは？」
lines.english: “Well? Your answer?”
“What?”
“Mmph.”

lines.japanese:
「...ごめん。
部活だったよな」
lines.english: “Sorry. The club, right.”

lines.japanese:
和泉の喋り方が舌足らずだったから
聞き取れなかった...訳じゃない。
lines.english: It wasn’t that the stem made her speech too blurred to understand.

lines.japanese: 「ええと...合唱部？」
lines.english: “The choir?”

lines.japanese: 「ぶぶー」
lines.english: “Wrong.”

lines.japanese:
その、顔と声と息遣いと舌の奏でる音が、
あまりにも艶めかしかったから。
lines.english: Her face, her voice, her breathing, the sounds made by her tongue—it was all far too sensuous.

lines.japanese:
「それなら...まさか軽音楽部とか。
そういうバンドのボーカルみたいな」
lines.english: “Then… the Light Music Club? Were you the singer in a band?”

lines.japanese: 「ぶぶー」
lines.english: “Wrong.”

lines.japanese:
小さくすぼめた唇からちろっと顔を出すピンクの舌とか、
少しだけ苦しそうで少しだけ恍惚とした吐息とか。
lines.english: That flash of pink tongue slipping between her pursed lips. Those little breaths, half strained and half ecstatic.

lines.japanese:
「...わかった、演劇部だ！
あの連中も発声練習よくやってるもんなぁ」
lines.english: “I know—the drama club! Actors do vocal exercises all the time.”
“…Wrong.”

lines.japanese:
そんな、和泉とは思えない『色』にあてられて、
俺は、酒だけじゃない、熱い汗を噴き出させ...
lines.english: Overcome by a sensuality I could hardly associate with Izumi, I broke into a hot sweat that had nothing to do with the alcohol.

lines.japanese:
「っ...降参。
もういいだろ」
lines.english: “I give up. That’s enough.”

lines.japanese:
和泉の顔を、まともに見ていられなくなり、
だからヒントをこれ以上見ることもかなわず、
あえなく負けを認めた。
lines.english: I could no longer look her in the face, much less keep watching the hint. I conceded a miserable defeat.

lines.japanese:
「前にも言っただろ。
勉強ばっかで、イベントとか興味なかったって」
lines.english: “I told you before. I did nothing but study. I wasn’t interested in school events.”

lines.japanese: 「それは聞いたけどね」
lines.english: “You did tell me that.”

lines.japanese:
クイズ勝負に負けた後は、
当然のように『春希の学園時代は？』が続いた。
lines.english: Once I’d lost our little guessing game, the obvious next question was, “What were you like in high school, Haruki?”

lines.japanese:
「クラス委員とか、学園祭実行委員とか、裏実行委員とか、
裏方ばっかで、面白いネタなんか何も...」
lines.english: “I was always behind the scenes—class representative, festival committee, unofficial festival committee. There’s nothing interesting to tell.”

lines.japanese:
「え～、裏実行委員ってなんか面白そ～だよ。
どんなことすんの？」
lines.english: “An unofficial committee sounds interesting. What did you do?”

lines.japanese:
「別に大したことはしてないけど。
...付属のミスコン大会の運営くらいで」
lines.english: “Nothing remarkable. We helped run the Miss Houjou High pageant.”

lines.japanese:
「え～、ミス峰城大付ってあれだよね？
ミス峰城の予備選って言われてるけど、
下手すると本家よりもレベルが高いって言う...」
lines.english: “Miss Houjou High? The pageant they call the preliminary round for Miss Houjou University, except sometimes the contestants are even better than the university’s?”

lines.japanese:
「いや、俺ただの実行委員だったから、
世間の評判はよく知らないし」
lines.english: “I was only a committee member. I don’t know what the public thought of it.”

lines.japanese:
「そっか～、それでか～。
春希の女の子を見る目が妙に肥えてるのは～」
lines.english: “Now I understand why you have such discerning taste in women.”

lines.japanese: 「...俺がいつそんなエピソードを披露した？」
lines.english: “When have I ever given you evidence of that?”

lines.japanese:
だから俺は、酒のせいで口が軽くなった『ふり』をして、
原点に立ち返って、和泉との軽口を楽しもうとした。
lines.english: So I pretended the alcohol had loosened my tongue and tried to get us back where we belonged: trading easy jabs with each other.

lines.japanese:
「それでそれで？
春希が委員やってた頃は、誰が優勝したの？
その子と親しかった？」
lines.english: “Well? Who won when you were on the committee? Were you close to her?”

lines.japanese:
「和泉の知らないコだよ。
確かこの大学にいるけど、俺も詳しくは...」
lines.english: “No one you know. I think she attends this university, but I don’t really know anything about her.”

lines.japanese:
あくまで『ふり』だから、
心の中身を全部さらす訳じゃないけれど。
lines.english: Because it was only a performance, I had no intention of revealing everything inside me.

lines.japanese:
「ふぅん...
ねぇ、付き合ったりしなかったの？
裏実行委員の特権を利用して、とか」
lines.english: “Really? You didn’t date her? Abuse your special committee privileges?”

lines.japanese: 「そういうのは思いっきり選挙違反だろ」
lines.english: “That would be blatant election fraud.”

lines.japanese: だから途中で辞任したんだっけ...
lines.english: Which was why I’d resigned halfway through, wasn’t it?

lines.japanese:
「あ、そいえばさ、
ギター、いつ頃までやってたの？
ほら、部屋に飾ってあったやつ」
lines.english: “Oh, that reminds me. How long did you play guitar? The one hanging in your room.”
“…I don’t remember.”

lines.japanese:
心の中をいくら隠し通しても、
自分に反動が返ってくることは避けようがない。
lines.english: The better I hid what I felt, the harder it rebounded on me.

lines.japanese:
そして、心の中を隠し通してるせいで、
相手を責めるわけにも、泣き言を言うわけにもいかない。
lines.english: And because I’d hidden it all from her, I had no right to blame her or complain.

lines.japanese:
そんな俺の、心の揺らぎに気づいたのか、
和泉がまた、じっと俺の顔を覗き込む。
lines.english: Perhaps she sensed me wavering, because Izumi leaned in and studied my face again.

lines.japanese:
だから俺は、
自分が心を開ききっていないことを隠すため、
さり気なく、その視線から距離を置き...
lines.english: I eased away from her gaze, trying not to let her see how much I was still holding back…

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、春希」
lines.english: “Hey, Haruki.”

lines.japanese: 「...なんだよ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「あんた、さっきからちっともあたしの方見ないよね？」
lines.english: “You haven’t looked at me this whole time.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
なんて、今になって行動したと思ってたのは、
自分の方だけだったみたいだ。
lines.english: Apparently I was the only one who thought I’d only just started avoiding her eyes.

lines.japanese:
「いっつも『人と話す時は相手の顔を見て喋れ』って、
えっらそうに説教する癖にさ」
lines.english: “And you’re always lecturing me to look at people when I talk to them.”

lines.japanese: 「それは、その...悪い」
lines.english: “You’re right. Sorry.”

lines.japanese:
そういえば俺は、
さっきからずっと和泉の顔を見ていない。
...ような気がする。
lines.english: Come to think of it, I hadn’t looked Izumi in the face for quite some time. Or at least, that was how it felt.

lines.japanese: 「どしたの？　そろそろ酔った？」
lines.english: “What’s wrong? Are you finally drunk?”

lines.japanese: 「...わからない」
lines.english: “I don’t know.”

lines.japanese: だって、いやでも感じてしまうから。
lines.english: Because I couldn’t help feeling her there.

lines.japanese:
「そろそろ帰る？
...家まで送ってこっか？」
lines.english: “Should we go home soon? Want me to see you home?”

lines.japanese:
「やめとく。
...そのまま泊まられそうだ」
lines.english: “No, thanks. You’d probably end up staying the night.”

lines.japanese:
和泉は、俺の顔を覗き込もうと、
カウンターに顔を伏せ、至近距離で見上げてる。
lines.english: Trying to catch my eye, Izumi had lowered her face to the counter and was gazing up at me from inches away.

lines.japanese: 「...春希ってテレパシー使い？」
lines.english: “Are you telepathic, Haruki?”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱりかよ...」
lines.english: “I knew it.”

lines.japanese:
スツールに腰掛けた体は俺の方にずれ、
その柔らかくて温かい体を
ぴっとりと俺の脇腹に張りつけてくる。
lines.english: She shifted closer on her stool until the soft warmth of her body pressed snugly against my side.

lines.japanese:
吐息は、俺の顎あたりに触れるように吐き出し、
唇と舌の奏でる音は、執拗に俺の右耳をねぶる。
lines.english: Her breath brushed my chin, while the sounds of her lips and tongue licked insistently at my right ear.

lines.japanese:
そして見上げた視線は、
潤んだまま、俺の目の辺りにまっすぐに突き刺さり、
まるで誘っているような...
lines.english: Her glistening eyes looked straight up into mine, as if she were inviting me…
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 「ど、どうした？」
lines.english: “Wh-what is it?”

lines.japanese:
「...結べた。
サクランボの茎」
lines.english: “I tied it. The cherry stem.”
“…Congratulations.”

lines.japanese: 「んふふ...記念にあげる」
lines.english: “Hee-hee. You can have it as a souvenir.”

lines.japanese: 「いるかそんなの」
lines.english: “Why would I want that?”

lines.japanese:
なんて、俺の勘違いと妄想を断ち切ってくれたのは、
やっぱり和泉のなんでもない軽口だった。
lines.english: Once again, an idle joke from Izumi rescued me from my own delusions and misunderstandings.

lines.japanese:
「うん、出よか。
あたしもそろそろ終電ヤバいし」
lines.english: “Let’s go. I’m in danger of missing the last train.”
“Right… Oh.”

lines.japanese: 「どしたの？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「...何でもない」
lines.english: “Nothing.”

lines.japanese:
でも、いくら俺の妄想と勘違いが、
相当に痛いものであったとしても。
lines.english: Yet no matter how embarrassingly deluded I might have been,

lines.japanese:
今まで、ずっと握り合ったままだった手は、
誰が、どう言い訳すればいいんだろうか...
lines.english: who could explain away the fact that our hands had remained clasped all this time?

lines.japanese: 「寒いね～」
lines.english: “Cold, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「冷えるね～」
lines.english: “Sure is chilly.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Mm.”

lines.japanese: 「意味、同じだね～」
lines.english: “Those mean the same thing.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだな」
lines.english: “Pretty much.”
“Pfft…”

lines.japanese:
和泉の言う通り、
あれだけ飲んでいたにもかかわらず、
外は肌寒く、底冷えして、それって同じ意味だった。
lines.english: Izumi was right. Despite everything we’d drunk, the air outside was cold on the skin and cold in the bones—which meant the same thing.

lines.japanese: 「ね、春希は冬休み、どうするの？」
lines.english: “What are you doing over winter break, Haruki?”

lines.japanese: 「またか」
lines.english: “That again?”

lines.japanese: 「前にも聞いたっけ？　同じ事」
lines.english: “Did I ask you before?”

lines.japanese: 「...気のせいかも」
lines.english: “Maybe I imagined it.”

lines.japanese:
和泉を送るために上がったホームでは、
肌を刺す冷たい空気が、吐息まで白く濁らせ、
一気に酔いを覚ましていく。
lines.english: On the platform where I’d gone to see Izumi off, the air bit at my skin and clouded every breath, driving the alcohol from my head all at once.

lines.japanese:
けれど、そんな寒さの中、
一箇所だけ、温かさが失われない場所がある。
lines.english: Yet amid all that cold, one place had not lost its warmth.

lines.japanese: 和泉の左手に包まれた、俺の右手。
lines.english: My right hand, wrapped in Izumi’s left.

lines.japanese:
「別に、会おうとか遊ぼうとか、
あたしの方からは誘わないけどさ...」
lines.english: “I won’t be the one asking you to meet up or hang out…”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese:
「でも、ま、異様にヒマだったり、
心がどうにも落ち着かなくなっちゃったりした時には、
遠慮なく呼び出してくれていいからね？」
lines.english: “But if you ever get desperately bored, or too restless to know what to do with yourself, you can always call me, okay?”
“Izumi…”

lines.japanese:
そんな、これだけ近づいてしまったのに、
それでもちょっとあっさりめの距離感が、
相変わらず心地良い。
lines.english: Even after we’d grown this close, she still kept things easy and undemanding between us. As always, it felt good.

lines.japanese:
「６番線、有川行きが参ります。
ご注意ください」
lines.english: “The train for Arikawa is arriving on Track Six. Please stand clear.”

lines.japanese:
だから、もうすぐ電車が来て、
俺の体のどこも温かくなくなってしまうことが、
なんだか辛いって、そんな、酷い心配をしてる。
lines.english: And so I found myself dreading the train—dreading the moment its arrival would leave no part of me warm.

lines.japanese:
「春希のお望みのあたしが相手するよ？
親友でも、悪友でも...それとも...」
lines.english: “Whatever version of me you want will keep you company—your best friend, your partner in crime… or perhaps…”

lines.japanese: そう、そんな心配は酷いこと。
lines.english: Yes. It was a terrible thing to dread.

lines.japanese:
また誰をも裏切る、また誰も幸せにしない、
そんな、最低最悪の選択肢。
lines.english: Another choice that would betray someone, another choice that could make no one happy—the vilest choice of all.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ」
lines.english: “Well, then…”
“Y-yeah…”
“Haruki?”
“Oh! Sorry, I…”

lines.japanese:
そして俺は、
自ら、そんな最低最悪の答えを引き寄せる。
lines.english: And with my own hand, I drew that vile answer closer.

lines.japanese: 「そうだよねぇ」
lines.english: “I thought so.”
“N-no—that’s not…”

lines.japanese: 和泉が、俺の胸に体を寄せる。
lines.english: Izumi leaned against my chest.

lines.japanese:
だって彼女は、
そうするより他になかったから。
lines.english: Because she had no other choice.

lines.japanese: 「しばらく、会えないもんねぇ」
lines.english: “We won’t see each other for a while.”

lines.japanese: 「和泉ぃ...っ」
lines.english: “Izumi…!”

lines.japanese:
俺に強く手を握られて、
振りほどくこともできないんだから。
lines.english: I was gripping her hand too tightly for her to pull away.

lines.japanese: 「んふふ...春希ってばさぁ」
lines.english: “Hee-hee… Haruki, you…”
“No, I…”

lines.japanese:
俺はもう、和泉の
『女っぽくないこと』を必要としていない。
lines.english: I no longer needed Izumi to seem unfeminine.

lines.japanese:
以前みたいに、こいつのこと、
女除けみたいに使う必要だってない。
lines.english: I no longer needed to use her as a shield against other women, as I once had.

lines.japanese:
今の俺は、自分のあるがままを受け入れ、
段々、昔みたいに女性と接することができてきてる。
lines.english: I had begun to accept myself as I was. Little by little, I was learning to be around women the way I had before.

lines.japanese: 「冗談...だよな？」
lines.english: “You’re joking… right?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese:
「ドアが閉まります。
ご注意ください」
lines.english: “The doors are closing. Please stand clear.”

lines.japanese: なのになぜ...
lines.english: Then why?

lines.japanese: 今こうして和泉の『女』を受け入れてるんだ、俺？
lines.english: Why was I accepting Izumi as a woman now?

lines.japanese:
俺が和泉に『女』を求めてるから？
それが本当に俺が欲しかったものだったのか？
lines.english: Was it because I wanted her as a woman? Was that what I had truly wanted?

lines.japanese:
どうして？
だって俺は...
lines.english: Why? Because I…

lines.japanese: 「冗談だけどね」
lines.english: “Only joking, though.”
“Yeah… of course it was.”

lines.japanese: 俺は...
lines.english: I was…
